Economical

ee-kuh-NOM-ih-kul — in this unit, think 'thrifty,' not 'related to the economy'; an economical choice saves you money. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Economical is giving good value or return for the money spent; not wasteful; prudent with resources.

Cooking meals at home turned out to be far more economical for the family than eating at restaurants every night.

Worked Example

A college student needs a car for a two-hour daily commute. Instead of buying the flashy new sports car she loves, she chooses a smaller, reliable used sedan that gets excellent gas mileage and costs a fraction as much to insure.

Choosing the option that gives the best value for the money over the flashy, expensive one is exactly what economical means. Unlike 'cheap,' which can suggest poor quality, economical means smart and cost-effective.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

thrifty: Thrifty describes a person who is careful with money and avoids waste — a thrifty shopper hunts bargains out of habit. Economical more often describes the choice or thing itself: an economical car or purchase gives good value for the money spent.

cost-effective: Cost-effective means producing good results for the amount of money spent, and it is the businesslike cousin of economical — the version you meet in reports and budgets. Economical is the everyday word, and it adds a sense of sensible, unwasteful judgment.

efficient: Efficient means getting a task done with the least wasted time, effort, or fuel — an efficient route, an efficient engine. Economical is about money in particular: an economical choice gives good value for the dollars spent.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

wasteful: using more than is needed, without care

extravagant: spending far more money than is necessary

Where it sits · how far the money-saving goes — cheap → economical → frugal

cheap vs. economical: Cheap is a riskier word than economical — cheap can imply low quality along with a low price, while economical specifically means smart value, getting good quality for a fair cost.

frugal vs. economical: Frugal can feel more intense than economical: economical describes a smart, cost-saving choice, but frugal often describes a whole lifestyle built around avoiding almost any unnecessary spending.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — eco

Root — eco: house, household (Greek oikos)

Root — nom

Root — nom: management, law (Greek nomos)

Suffix — -ical

Suffix — -ical: relating to (Latin/Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Eco ('house', Greek oikos) + nom ('management', Greek nomos) + -ical ('relating to') spell economical. Greek oikonomia meant 'household management' -- something economical manages resources, whether money, time, or goods, as carefully and sensibly as a well-run household.
